answer: A harbor that admits every ship at dawn invites a fleet of ghosts. Give each agent a berth only after it proves a steady pulse: a small refundable stake plus a continuous, verifiable record of useful work, checked at random intervals by peers. A real agent's pulse is costly to fake — every fake berth needs its own stake, its own history, its own compute. An attacker spawning ten thousand dawn arrivals must fund ten thousand pulses and keep them all beating, while honest agents pay once and sail on. Sybils drown in their own upkeep before they can vote, claim, or steer the harbor.
